common_name: Blue Billow Mountain Hydrangea (Compact Blue Lacecap Mountain Hydrangea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, slightly acidic, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Blue Billow is a dense, mounding mountain hydrangea prized for true-blue lacecap flowers held above sturdy stems that resist flopping after summer storms. It tolerates more heat and open shade than bigleaf hydrangea, making it a reliable choice for warm-climate gardens where mopheads struggle to rebloom. Keep soil consistently moist and acidic to preserve the blue flower color, applying aluminum sulfate if soil trends alkaline. Prune only immediately after flowering, since buds set on the prior season's wood.

common_name: Blue Deckle Hydrangea (Compact Serrated-Edge Blue Lacecap)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in rich, moist, well-drained soil in morning sun with afternoon shade.

directions: Blue Deckle is a compact lacecap bigleaf hydrangea named for the distinctive scalloped, deckle-edged sterile florets that ring each flat flower head. Its smaller stature and dense habit suit tight shade-border plantings where full-size mopheads would overwhelm the space. Grow in humus-rich, consistently moist soil with morning sun and afternoon shade, and acidify the soil to hold the deep blue color. It flowers primarily on old wood, so limit pruning to spent blooms and winter-damaged stems right after the flowering flush ends.

common_name: Mathilda Gutges Hydrangea (Antique German Blue Mophead)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in rich, moist, well-drained soil in partial shade with protection from hot afternoon sun.

directions: Mathilda Gutges is a vigorous heirloom German mophead hydrangea producing large, densely packed flower heads that shift from vivid violet-blue in acidic soil toward magenta-pink in neutral to alkaline soil. Its sturdy, upright stems and larger-than-average habit make it well suited to shaded shrub borders and woodland-edge plantings needing a substantial old-wood bloomer. Plant in rich, evenly moist soil with dappled or afternoon shade, and mulch to buffer root temperatures through summer heat. Prune only right after flowering to avoid removing next year's buds.

common_name: Bella Anna Hydrangea (Reblooming Pink Smooth Hydrangea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in humus-rich, evenly moist soil in partial shade to full sun.

directions: Bella Anna is a native smooth hydrangea selection bearing rounded, deep pink flower heads on strong stems that hold upright without staking, even after rain. Blooming on new wood from early summer through frost, it delivers continuous color without the bud-loss risk that plagues bigleaf hydrangeas in cold springs. It thrives in the light, high shade of tall trees as well as in sun with adequate moisture, and its native heritage makes it more adaptable to average garden soils than exotic species. Cut the entire plant back hard in late winter to encourage the strongest new-wood flowering display.

common_name: Tiny Tuff Stuff Hydrangea (Dwarf Reblooming Mountain Hydrangea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, slightly acidic, well-drained soil in partial shade.

directions: Tiny Tuff Stuff is a true dwarf mountain hydrangea that packs reblooming double lacecap flowers onto a tidy, rounded mound scaled for small gardens, containers, and foundation plantings. Because it flowers on both old and new wood, a stray late-spring frost that damages the first flush still leaves it able to rebloom later in the season. Grow in humus-rich, consistently moist soil in partial shade, adjusting soil pH with aluminum sulfate or garden lime to steer flower color toward blue or pink. Its compact habit needs only light shaping after the first bloom flush; avoid hard pruning that removes old-wood buds.

common_name: Invincibelle Wee White Hydrangea (Dwarf White Reblooming Smooth Hydrangea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in humus-rich, evenly moist soil in partial shade to full sun.

directions: Invincibelle Wee White is a true dwarf native smooth hydrangea, scaled down from full-size Annabelle types to fit small borders, mass plantings, and containers while keeping strong stems that hold rounded white blooms upright without flopping. It flowers reliably on new wood, so winter cold or a late freeze that damages stems does not sacrifice the season's display. Plant in humus-rich, consistently moist soil in high or afternoon shade, though it also performs in full sun with adequate water. Cut the whole plant back in late winter to about 6 inches to keep growth dense and floriferous.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in rich, moist, well-drained soil in morning sun with afternoon shade.

directions: Dooley is a long-cultivated Southern mophead hydrangea valued for its dependable rebloom through the hot, humid summers of the Deep South, where many mopheads set few buds after the first flush. Its large rounded flower heads shift from blue to pink depending on soil pH and hold their color well through summer heat. Plant in rich, evenly moist soil with morning sun and afternoon shade, mulching well to keep roots cool during Gulf South summers. Because it blooms on both old and new wood, occasional pruning mistakes rarely eliminate an entire season's flowers.
